name: Photocatalytic and thermochemical water splitting
principle: Sunlight splits water directly: photocatalytic and photoelectrochemical devices use photons, while solar thermochemical cycles use concentrated heat (for example a metal-oxide cycle with doped ceria). IEA rates photon-based direct solar water splitting at TRL 5 and solar or nuclear thermochemical water splitting at TRL 4. Pilots include Sparc Hydrogen (photocatalytic, Australia), SunHydrogen (a pilot of about 15 PEC panels) and CSIRO's beam-down reactor.
